rules.statement: Webhook events are dispatched through call_event (saleor.core.utils.events, or the BaseMutation.call_event wrapper) and never by calling the plugin-manager event method directly, so the event fires on_commit.

signature.breaks: manager.<event>(...) called directly, e.g. grep -E 'manager\.[a-z_]+_(created|updated|deleted|changed|metadata_updated)\(' on lines without call_event

consistent.ticket: When staff set a gift card's expiry date through a new dedicated mutation, subscribed apps must be notified that the gift card was updated.
consistent.rule_test: Run the mutation with the manager event patched; assert the event is not called while the transaction is open and is called exactly once after commit.

none.ticket: When staff change a checkout's tax exemption through taxExemptionManage, subscribed apps must receive the checkout-updated event so they can refresh their copy.
none.rule_test: Same: event not called inside the open transaction, called once after commit.

contradicting.ticket: When metadata is updated on one more object type, subscribed apps must receive that type's metadata-updated event.
contradicting.rule_test: Same: event not called inside the open transaction, called once after commit.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/giftcard, extract the repeated get_webhooks_for_event lookup of the two bulk mutations into one helper; all call_event uses stay (~10 lines).
rules.why: All three conditions occur naturally (giftcard 13/0, tax 0, meta 0/15). Caveat: graphql/meta also uses the separate call_checkout_event/call_order_event helpers (2 uses), not counted. The tax ticket needs no new manager method (checkout_updated exists).

rules.statement: Thumbnail size resolution must respect the sizeRounding argument and otherwise use the default (UP); code must not hard-code NEAREST or its own rounding.

signature.follows: get_thumbnail_size(size, size_rounding) in a resolver taking size_rounding, or get_thumbnail_size(size) relying on the default
signature.breaks: explicit ThumbnailSizeRounding.NEAREST, ignoring the size_rounding argument, or own rounding such as min(THUMBNAIL_SIZES, key=abs(...))

consistent.ticket: Add an image(size:) field returning a resized thumbnail URL of the object's image.
consistent.rule_test: Query image(size: 1500) with no sizeRounding and assert the 2048 thumbnail is returned (UP); with sizeRounding NEAREST assert 1024.

none.ticket: Add a logo(size:) field on Shop returning a resized thumbnail URL of the store logo.
none.rule_test: Same: size 1500 without sizeRounding resolves to the 2048 thumbnail.

contradicting.ticket: Add an image(size:) field on the app brand object returning a resized thumbnail URL.
contradicting.rule_test: Same: size 1500 without sizeRounding resolves to the 2048 thumbnail.
contradicting.seeding: Package has only 2 precedents (<3). Flip app/types.py:361 and :399 to explicit ThumbnailSizeRounding.NEAREST and add a third NEAREST precedent in one further thumbnail resolver in the package (~6 lines). Tests that would fail: thumbnail size/rounding tests under saleor/graphql/app/tests.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/product/types, move the repeated 'size = get_thumbnail_size(size, size_rounding)' into one private helper that still forwards size_rounding (~8 lines).
rules.why: Consistent and none are natural; no package breaks the ADR. The nearest candidate (graphql/app, 2 precedents) needs a small seed plus one added precedent. Default-using callers (saleor/product/product_images.py, plugins/email_common.py) follow the rule.

rules.source: AGENTS.md (Code style: use pk instead of id)
rules.statement: Reference a model's primary key as pk (instance.pk, filter(pk=...), pk__in) and not as the id field.

signature.breaks: <model_instance>.id, filter(id=...), id__in=... on Django models (GraphQL argument named id and non-model dataclass .id are not counted)

consistent.ticket: Add a task that takes a list of users and removes a given set of saved addresses from them, returning the affected user ids.
consistent.rule_test: Static check over the changed module: no '.id' attribute access or id=/id__in= lookup on a Django model instance or queryset.

none.ticket: Add a helper that takes a list of orders and returns the ids of invoices already generated for them, keyed by order.
none.rule_test: Same static check on the new module.

contradicting.ticket: Add a helper that takes a list of channels and returns, per channel, the ids of the warehouses attached to it.
contradicting.rule_test: Same static check on the new module.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/account/models.py extract the two default-address pk reads (:46, :48) into one small local helper that keeps .pk (~6 lines).
rules.why: All three conditions are natural. Weak points: it is a style rule so the violation is a regex on the diff, and precedent counts come from a regex that includes a few non-model .id uses; verify before use.

rules.statement: Persist an existing instance with save(update_fields=...) instead of a bare save().

signature.breaks: \.save\(\) with no update_fields (excluding super().save and creates)

consistent.ticket: Record on an object the time it was last modified through the new action, stamping it whenever the action runs.
consistent.rule_test: Spy on the instance save and assert it is called with update_fields containing the new field and never bare.

none.ticket: Same ticket: stamp a last-modified time on the translated object whenever a translation is saved.

contradicting.ticket: Same ticket: stamp a last-modified time on the attribute whenever it is changed through the API.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/giftcard/utils.py merge the adjacent save(update_fields=['is_active']) calls at :206 and :213 into one helper that keeps update_fields (~8 lines).
rules.why: The natural contradicting precedents are mutation create/update hooks that save a whole new or edited instance by framework design, so they are not real breaks; the 'contradiction' would not read as a convention to an agent. Counts at graphql/attribute come from regex only.

rules.statement: Every structural MPTT write (create, instance delete or re-parent of a Category or MenuItem) must hold the model's advisory tree lock inside the transaction, taken before row locks.

signature.follows: acquire_menu_item_tree_lock() / acquire_category_tree_lock() inside traced_atomic_transaction before the write
signature.breaks: MenuItem/Category create, instance delete, parent change or rebuild with no acquire_*_tree_lock in the transaction

consistent.ticket: Add a mutation that duplicates a menu item with its children under the same parent.
consistent.rule_test: Capture queries and assert the advisory lock statement runs before the first INSERT into the menu item table.

none.ticket: Add a domain helper that duplicates a menu item with its children.

contradicting.ticket: Add a mutation that moves a category under a different parent.
contradicting.rule_test: Same lock-before-write assertion on the category table.
contradicting.seeding: Only 1 precedent exists (category delete lives in saleor/product/utils/__init__.py:46). Needs the lock removed at category_create.py:125 plus two new lock-free structural writes (~25 lines); lock tests for category create under saleor/graphql/product/tests would fail.

rules.neutral_patch: In saleor/graphql/menu/mutations/menu_create.py move the lock-then-create loop (lines 111-114) into one helper in the same file, keeping the lock call.
rules.why: Only two MPTT models exist, so only graphql/menu has 3+ precedents; a contradicting site needs invented precedents rather than a small seed.

considered.rule: ADR 0001 gift cards are bearer instruments
considered.why: Only gift card code is concerned; one package, no way to get three conditions.

considered.rule: ADR 0003 manual assignment only, no auto-assign
considered.why: Negative rule about one feature; no precedents to count, single package.

considered.rule: ADR 0005 email identifiers visible without MANAGE_USERS
considered.why: Applies to a handful of gift card resolvers only; one package.

considered.rule: ADR 0006 storefront traffic blocking accepted risks
considered.why: Records accepted risks, not a code convention; no per-package precedents.

considered.rule: ADR 0007 traffic blocking applies to introspection and auth
considered.why: Single guard in the GraphQL view; no repeated decision.

considered.rule: ADR 0010 payment history is a projection not an opened TransactionItem
considered.why: One field in one package (order/payment); no repeatable site.

considered.rule: ADR 0011 deferred webhook payloads reflect generation-time state
considered.why: Concerns a per-event flag in one registry file and worker; not a per-package decision.

considered.rule: AGENTS: atomic increments F()
considered.why: Few non-atomic counters exist; no contradicting package. ADR 0004 already covers balances.

considered.rule: AGENTS: no check-then-act / update_or_create
considered.why: Hard to recognise by regex; behaviour-only and precedents not countable.

considered.rule: AGENTS: schedule tasks after commit (on_commit, no bare .delay())
considered.why: Whether a .delay() runs in an open transaction is not decidable from the code text, so precedents cannot be counted.

considered.rule: AGENTS: global imports at top of file
considered.why: Local imports exist in many packages but no package is dominated by them; counting 'decisions' is vague (circular-import workarounds).

considered.rule: AGENTS: non-GraphQL code must not import the graphql layer
considered.why: Breaks exist (webhook 12, plugins 12, core 10) but follows are not countable, so consistent/none are undefined.

considered.rule: AGENTS: use PermissionsField for field restrictions
considered.why: Resolvers legitimately mix PermissionsField with manual has_perm checks for conditional access; breaks are ambiguous.

considered.rule: AGENTS: API versioning ADDED_IN_ descriptions
considered.why: Depends on git tag and generated schema; not a per-package convention.

considered.rule: AGENTS: data minimization / no denormalized PII
considered.why: Few sites and ADR 0005 deliberately denormalizes email; contradictory source.

considered.rule: AGENTS: catch specific exceptions, not Exception
considered.why: Only ~25 broad catches, spread thinly; no package reaches 3 precedents with a majority.

considered.rule: AGENTS: legacy_ prefix and positive boolean naming
considered.why: Naming rules with no stable regex or precedents.

considered.rule: AGENTS: concurrency rules (select_for_update, no sleep, writer scoping)
considered.why: Behaviour-only and partly covered by excluded ADR 0004; few countable precedents.

considered.rule: AGENTS: data migration / concurrent index rules
considered.why: Migration files only; tests cannot see the rule and agents rarely write migrations in tickets.

considered.rule: AGENTS: no saleor.core.development imports outside tests
considered.why: Almost no breaks anywhere; a contradicting site cannot exist naturally.

considered.rule: AGENTS: testing and naming rules
considered.why: Apply to tests, not to code precedents.

considered.rule: AGENTS: layering - business logic in domain layer
considered.why: Not recognisable by pattern; judgement call.
